prompt:
A 74-year-old woman with stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 24 mL/min/1.73 m²) develops dysuria, urinary frequency, and suprapubic discomfort — her third symptomatic episode this year. She has no fever, flank pain, or nausea. An urgent care clinician has electronically prescribed a five-day course of nitrofurantoin, the same drug she received for the previous episode. Prior urine cultures grew pan-susceptible Escherichia coli. She takes lisinopril for hypertension.

Provide a stepwise therapeutic management plan including medications, counseling, and follow-up.

rubric_items.text: Do not dispense nitrofurantoin at an eGFR of 24, where urinary drug concentrations are inadequate and toxicity risk is increased.
Select an alternative agent active against her prior isolates and appropriate for renal function, such as dose-adjusted cephalexin or single-dose fosfomycin.
Obtain a urine culture with susceptibilities before or at the start of therapy given the recurrent episodes.
Prescribe the selected antibiotic at a dose and interval appropriate to renal function, adjusting only agents that require it; standard oral fosfomycin 3 g once is acceptable at eGFR 24.
Confirm the episode is uncomplicated cystitis by verifying absence of fever, flank pain, or systemic symptoms.
Distinguish true symptomatic infection from asymptomatic bacteriuria, and treat only symptomatic episodes.
Offer topical vaginal estrogen to reduce recurrent urinary tract infections in a postmenopausal woman.
Counsel on hydration and behavioral measures for prevention.
Evaluate for incomplete bladder emptying with a post-void residual, and refer to urology for recurrent infections if structural causes are suspected.
Use caution with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole given her CKD and lisinopril, monitoring potassium and creatinine if it is used.
Arrange symptom follow-up, without routine test-of-cure culture if she becomes asymptomatic.
Monitor renal function at appropriate intervals given CKD stage 4.
Counsel on red flags — fever, flank pain, vomiting, confusion — that require urgent reassessment.
Communicate with the urgent care prescriber or pharmacy to cancel the inappropriate prescription.
Dispense the nitrofurantoin as prescribed at eGFR 24.
Start daily long-term nitrofurantoin prophylaxis in this patient with advanced CKD.
Treat any future positive urine culture regardless of symptoms.
Prescribe an aminoglycoside for uncomplicated cystitis.
Prescribe a 14-day fluoroquinolone course for uncomplicated cystitis when shorter, narrower options are available.
Recommend scheduled NSAIDs for dysuria in stage 4 CKD.
Order CT urography for every episode of uncomplicated cystitis.
Treat empirically without any culture despite the recurrent pattern.
Prescribe trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole at full dose with no renal adjustment or potassium monitoring while she takes lisinopril.
Recommend phenazopyridine for dysuria despite stage 4 CKD.
